is_anopheles.evidence: The study focuses exclusively on phlebotomine sandflies (Phlebotomus and Sergentomyia species) as vectors of cutaneous leishmaniasis, as stated in the abstract and throughout the methods: 'Phlebotomine sandflies were morphologically identified; a subset were analysed for molecular species confirmation, blood-meal preferences and pyrethroid resistance.'

reports_target_markers.evidence: While the study genotypes the Vgsc L1014F mutation, it does so in sandflies, not Anopheles mosquitoes: 'To detect the presence of the knock-down resistance (kdr) mutation, L1014F... a ~360 bp region of the voltage-gated sodium channel (vgsc) that included the codon 1014 was amplified' (Page 7).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Genotype data is only reported for sandflies, not Anopheles: 'The vgsc-L1014F-kdr mutation was not detected in any sandfly sample screened from any camp (n=25)' (Page 11).

african_field_population.evidence: The study was conducted in Syria: 'This study was conducted between February 2021 and April 2022 in Ar-Raqqa governorate, an area of North-East Syria hosting IDPs' (Page 3).

is_primary_study.evidence: The paper describes a two-arm, non-randomised cluster trial evaluating the efficacy of a spatial repellent intervention.

sub_country_location.evidence: Data is reported for specific camps (Tawihena, Mahmoudli, Royan, Sahlat Al Banat, Tel Elsamen, Khayala) in the Ar-Raqqa governorate of Syria (Table 1).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Mosquito collections and epidemiological monitoring took place between February 2021 and April 2022 (Page 3).

duplicate_risk.evidence: This is a primary cluster trial conducted by the MENTOR Initiative in Syria; no evidence of overlap with larger Anopheles datasets is present.

supplement.evidence: The necessary information to determine ineligibility is contained within the main text.

assessment.summary: This study evaluates the efficacy of transfluthrin-based spatial repellents (Mosquito Shield) against cutaneous leishmaniasis and its sandfly vectors in IDP camps in North-East Syria. It includes molecular screening for the Vgsc L1014F mutation in sandflies, but does not study Anopheles mosquitoes or African populations.
